strategy_summary:
This plan executes a bounded Anxiety of Influence thematic analysis with Otto Neurath as the fixed source thinker and Aaron Benanav's NLR dossier as the target corpus. The corpus configuration is ideal for thematic AOI: Benanav's two-part essay explicitly reconstructs socialist economic traditions with heavy reliance on Neurath's multi-criterial framework, calculation-in-kind arguments, and socialisation proposals, while Neurath's source corpus spans four major collections covering economic theory, socialisation policy, philosophy of science, and visual education — totaling approximately 3.6 million characters across 40 years of output.

The pipeline follows the canonical four-phase AOI structure. Phase 1.0 runs aoi_thematic_synthesis at deep depth over all four Neurath source works to capture the full breadth of his thematic world — critically including themes Benanav may strategically ignore (unified science epistemology, ISOTYPE visual methodology, anti-metaphysical philosophy of social science). Phase 2.0 maps Benanav's engagement theme by theme at standard depth, consuming the stable thematic inventory from Phase 1.0 alongside the target text. Phase 3.0 produces discrete sin findings at deep depth with source-text access to anchor each finding in paired target/source provenance. Phase 4.0 closes the bounded loop with a structured report. Opus handles Phases 1-3 given the density of both the source corpus and the engagement patterns; Phase 4.0 uses sonnet for structured report generation. No expansion into thinker discovery, hypothesis generation, or genealogical tracing is included.

The key analytical challenge is that Benanav's engagement with Neurath is both deep and selective: the target work explicitly foregrounds Neurath's multi-criterial economy and socialisation proposals while potentially backgrounding the epistemological infrastructure (logical empiricism, physicalism, unified science) that made Neurath's economic proposals intelligible on their own terms. The deep depth on Phases 1.0 and 3.0 ensures that both the full source thematic map and the nuanced sin findings — including strategic silences — are captured with adequate evidence.

phases.context_emphasis: Reconstruct the FULL thematic world of Otto Neurath across all four source collections. Capture not only economic planning themes (economy in kind, calculation in kind, socialisation, administrative economy, central economic administration) but also epistemological themes (unified science, physicalism, logical empiricism, anti-metaphysics), methodological themes (ISOTYPE, visual education, picture language, empirical sociology), and political themes (international planning for freedom, democratic coordination, war economy as planning laboratory). Build a source-document inventory preserving stable source_document_id values for each work. Surface internal tensions between Neurath's positions across decades — early vs. late planning proposals, shifts in confidence about calculation feasibility, evolving relationship between epistemological and economic commitments.
phases.rationale: Foundation phase: reconstructs Neurath's full thematic world from all four source works. Deep depth is essential because Neurath's corpus is exceptionally dense (3.6M chars), internally complex (spanning 1904-1945), and thematically heterogeneous — covering economic theory, socialisation policy, philosophy of science, visual methodology, and social theory. Deep depth captures the internal tensions and second-order qualifications (e.g., Neurath's evolving position on whether calculation in kind can be formalized vs. must remain multi-criterial) that are precisely where AOI sins tend to cluster. Opus is required for the volume and conceptual density of the source material. No upstream dependencies — this is the root phase. Its output (theme inventory, claim structure, source-document inventory with stable IDs) feeds all downstream phases as the fixed comparison surface.

phases.context_emphasis: Map Benanav's engagement with each Neurath theme identified in Phase 1.0, attending carefully to the two-part structure of the target: Part 1 (Groundwork) traces socialist economic traditions historically and will show heavier direct engagement with Neurath's socialisation theory and calculation debate themes; Part 2 (Institutions) proposes concrete institutional designs and may draw on Neurath's administrative economy proposals while potentially diverging on mechanism. Pay special attention to strategic silences — themes from Neurath's corpus that are conspicuously absent from Benanav's treatment despite their centrality to Neurath's project (e.g., unified science epistemology, ISOTYPE methodology, physicalism as basis for social science). Classify engagement levels precisely: genuine grappling vs. selective citation vs. gestural reference vs. absence.
phases.rationale: Receives the stable theme inventory and source-document inventory from Phase 1.0 and maps Benanav's target text against it theme by theme. Standard depth is appropriate because the target work is relatively focused (274K chars, two-part essay) and the engagement patterns are likely to be clear once the thematic map is in hand — the key challenge is comprehensiveness rather than depth of excavation per theme. Opus is warranted because the engagement mapping must hold the full Phase 1.0 synthesis (which at deep depth will be extensive) alongside the target text and produce precise per-theme classifications. The phase consumes Phase 1.0 output as structured context and the target text as primary input. Its output — the engagement map — feeds both Phase 3.0 (as the basis for sin identification) and Phase 4.0 (as the structural backbone of the report).

phases.context_emphasis: Identify discrete AOI findings anchored to Phase 1.0 themes and Phase 2.0 engagement levels. For each finding, classify exactly one dominant sin type, assign severity, and preserve paired target-side and source-side provenance with source_document_id values from the Phase 1.0 inventory. Pay particular attention to: (1) selective appropriation — where Benanav takes Neurath's multi-criterial framework but strips away the epistemological commitments (unified science, physicalism) that grounded it; (2) modernization distortion — where Benanav translates Neurath's proposals into contemporary institutional forms (investment boards, dual monetary system) in ways that may alter their logic; (3) strategic silence — where Benanav's treatment of socialist calculation omits Neurath's explicit anti-monetary stance or his war economy reasoning; (4) genealogical flattening — where Neurath's evolving positions across decades are presented as a single stable position. Also capture any findings where Benanav's engagement is notably faithful or where he extends Neurath productively.
phases.rationale: The core evidential phase: produces flat, evidence-bearing AOI findings. Deep depth is critical here because Benanav's engagement with Neurath is both substantive and nuanced — there will be clear primary findings (e.g., around calculation in kind and multi-criterial evaluation) but also weaker secondary findings (e.g., around Neurath's visual methodology, his anti-metaphysical commitments, or his specific institutional proposals for central economic administration) that deep depth captures. Opus is necessary for the discriminating classification work — distinguishing legitimate extension from distortion, identifying what sin type best characterizes each divergence, and matching target-side passages to source-side evidence across a 3.6M char source corpus. Consumes Phase 1.0 thematic synthesis (as the theme anchor for each finding), Phase 2.0 engagement map (as the engagement-level context that guides where to look for sins), and raw source texts (for provenance extraction). Outputs the finding inventory that Phase 4.0 synthesizes.

phases.context_emphasis: Synthesize the overall AOI portrait: what is the dominant engagement pattern across themes? Which divergences matter most for how a reader should interpret Benanav's use of Neurath? Organize the report to serve the bounded thematic scope — do not gesture toward further thinker discovery or multi-thinker comparison. Highlight the most consequential findings (likely around the epistemological stripping of the multi-criterial framework and the institutional translation of socialisation proposals) while also noting where engagement is faithful. Close with reading implications: how should a reader who knows Neurath's full corpus interpret Benanav's appropriation?
phases.rationale: Report closeout: draws a bounded interpretive conclusion from all upstream outputs. Consumes Phase 1.0 thematic synthesis (for the source framework), Phase 2.0 engagement map (for the theme-by-theme engagement pattern), and Phase 3.0 sin findings (for the specific AOI evidence). Standard depth is sufficient because the analytical work is already complete — this phase synthesizes and structures rather than discovers. Sonnet is adequate for structured report generation given that all evidential and analytical content has been produced upstream. No raw documents needed — works entirely from Phase 1-3 outputs.

recommended_views.rationale: The parent AOI surface for the single-thinker thematic tranche. Its child views (aoi_source_documents, aoi_by_theme, aoi_by_sin_type, aoi_thematic_report) are auto-included by the presenter, providing the complete bounded AOI reading surface: source document inventory, theme-keyed engagement, sin-type-keyed findings, and the structured report.

estimated_depth_profile: Phase 1.0 runs deep (capturing 40 years of Neurath across 4 works with internal tensions and full thematic breadth), Phase 2.0 runs standard (focused engagement classification against the stable thematic map), Phase 3.0 runs deep (capturing primary and secondary sin findings with full provenance), Phase 4.0 runs standard (structured synthesis of upstream analytical outputs). Opus handles the three analytically demanding phases; sonnet handles report generation.

book_samples.title: round5-proof-dossier-final-1774100000
book_samples.structural_notes: Two-part essay series published in New Left Review (NLR 153 and 154, 2025). Part 1 ('Groundwork') is historically and theoretically oriented, tracing socialist economic traditions from 19th-century utopians through Soviet planning, Red Vienna, guild socialism, and Keynesian welfare state, with particular attention to Neurath's multi-criterial framework and the socialist calculation debate. Part 2 ('Institutions') is architecturally prospective, proposing concrete institutional arrangements (dual monetary system, data matrix, investment boards, worker-run firms, universal provision, technical associations). Both parts are heavily footnoted with engagement of academic literature across economics, political theory, and planning theory. The dossier also contains a closing section of URL references suggesting it is a compiled research dossier rather than a standalone publication.
book_samples.rationale: This is a systematic, historically grounded political-economy essay series developing an original theoretical framework ('multi-criterial economy') by engaging and synthesizing prior socialist and Keynesian traditions; it is best served by engines that map conceptual architecture, trace intellectual genealogies, and analyze argument structure. The high density of named thinkers (Neurath, Schumpeter, Devine, Schweickart, Keynes, Sen, Nussbaum) and cited works makes genealogical and concept-appropriation analysis especially productive.

book_samples.domain: history of economic thought / philosophy of social science / political economy
book_samples.structural_notes: Edited scholarly collection spanning 1904–1945, organized into four thematic parts: economic history, theory of economics and social science, socialisation theory, and economics within unified science. Prefaced by a substantial critical introduction by Uebel and preceded by an editors' and translators' note. Individual essays range from historical studies to theoretical interventions to policy proposals. The structure reflects both chronological and thematic organization across four decades of Neurath's work.
book_samples.rationale: This is a scholarly edited collection of Otto Neurath's economic writings spanning four decades, combining historical analysis, institutional economics, socialist planning theory, and Vienna Circle philosophy of science; it is highly relevant to concept tracking (economy in kind, socialisation, unified science), intellectual genealogy, and epistemological/methodological analysis of how logical empiricism intersected with heterodox political economy.

book_samples.title: Modern Man in the Making   Otto Neurath   A. A. Knopf   1939
book_samples.domain: social science / visual statistics / sociology of modernity
book_samples.structural_notes: The book is organized as a heavily illustrated survey of global social conditions, combining statistical charts (isotype pictograms) with short expository prose passages. Sections move thematically across topics such as class, housing, health, and social stratification. Endnotes cite supporting studies (e.g., Middletown). The foreword explicitly frames the methodology and the picture-text hybrid form. The work is closer to a data-journalism compendium or public-education document than a conventional academic monograph.
book_samples.rationale: Neurath's work is a hybrid popular-scientific atlas of global modernity, methodologically distinctive for its isotype visual language and empiricist, anti-theoretical stance rooted in Vienna Circle logical empiricism; it is most relevant as a prior work for tracing concept genealogy (visualization, unified science, social fact) and for understanding the methodological and epistemological commitments Neurath brought to social statistics.

book_samples.structural_notes: Collected papers spanning 1913-1946, organized chronologically and thematically into numbered chapters, with editorial preface by Robert S. Cohen situating Neurath's contributions, bibliography of Neurath in English, and full index of names. Each paper is a self-contained essay addressing philosophy of science, unified science, physicalism, or related topics.
book_samples.rationale: This is a canonical collection of philosophical essays from a founding Vienna Circle member, centrally concerned with logical empiricism, physicalism, unified science, and the philosophy of scientific language—making it highly relevant to concept tracking, epistemological method detection, and argument architecture analysis. Its historical range (1913–1946) and anticipatory arguments (prefiguring Kuhn, pragmatic turn, etc.) make genealogical and comparative reasoning engines especially applicable.

phase_decisions.selection_rationale: The dedicated AOI engine for reconstructing a source thinker's thematic world. Directly serves the first primary goal. Its two dimensions (theme_inventory and claim_structure) at deep depth produce exactly the output needed: a comprehensive theme map with claims, commitments, and source-document provenance.
phase_decisions.depth_rationale: Deep depth is essential for three reasons: (1) the source corpus is exceptionally large (3.6M chars) and internally complex, spanning four decades of Neurath's work; (2) Neurath's positions evolved significantly over time (early war economy proposals vs. later multi-criterial framework), and deep depth captures these internal tensions; (3) the objective requires themes beyond the obvious economic ones — epistemological commitments, visual methodology, anti-metaphysical philosophy — which deep depth ensures are surfaced alongside the primary economic themes.
phase_decisions.iteration_mode_rationale: Single iteration processes all four source works together to produce a unified thematic synthesis, which is the correct approach for building a stable comparison surface across the full corpus.
alternatives_considered: concept_analysis_suite — rejected: genealogy-oriented chain that would profile concepts rather than reconstruct thematic claims and commitments

phase_decisions.selection_rationale: The dedicated AOI engine for mapping subject-corpus engagement against the source thematic synthesis. Its two dimensions (engagement_inventory and divergence_character) produce exactly the theme-by-theme engagement classification needed for downstream sin finding.
phase_decisions.depth_rationale: Standard depth is appropriate because the target work is relatively focused (274K chars, two parts) and the engagement patterns will be clear once the thematic map is available. The key challenge is comprehensiveness (covering all themes including those Benanav ignores) rather than per-theme excavation depth.
phase_decisions.iteration_mode_rationale: Single iteration maps the entire target corpus against all source themes in one pass, which is the correct approach for producing a coherent engagement map.
alternatives_considered: concept_appropriation_tracker — rejected: genealogy-specific engine focused on concept migration rather than thematic engagement classification

phase_decisions.dependency_rationale: Depends on Phase 1.0 which provides the stable theme inventory and source-document inventory. Phase 2.0 receives this synthesis as structured context and maps the target text against it. The Phase 1.0 output defines what counts as a 'theme' for engagement classification — without it, Phase 2.0 would have no stable comparison surface.

phase_decisions.selection_rationale: The dedicated AOI engine for identifying discrete sin findings. Its two dimensions (finding_identification and provenance) produce exactly the bounded, evidence-bearing findings required: each with one dominant sin type, severity, and paired target/source provenance.
phase_decisions.depth_rationale: Deep depth is essential because Benanav's engagement with Neurath is substantive enough that sin findings will span a range from clear-cut (strategic omission of epistemological framework) to nuanced (whether institutional translations constitute legitimate extension or distortion). Deep depth captures the weaker but meaningful secondary findings that standard depth would miss.
phase_decisions.iteration_mode_rationale: Single iteration examines all findings across the full theme inventory in one pass, which is correct for producing a coherent finding set with consistent severity calibration.
alternatives_considered: concept_appropriation_tracker — rejected: tracks migration and distortion but lacks AOI sin-type classification and bounded finding format

The engine also accesses raw source texts for evidence extraction, which is why requires_full_documents is true.

phase_decisions.selection_rationale: The dedicated AOI engine for report closeout. Its single dimension (summary) produces the structured thematic report deliverable, synthesizing the engagement pattern and sin findings into an interpretive conclusion.
phase_decisions.depth_rationale: Standard depth is sufficient because the analytical work is complete — this phase synthesizes and structures rather than discovers. The report quality depends on the richness of upstream outputs, which deep depth on Phases 1.0 and 3.0 ensures.

The report synthesizes these three streams into a coherent interpretive document.

decision_trace.overall_strategy_rationale: The pipeline is a clean four-phase bounded AOI workflow, closely following the canonical baseline but with strategic depth and model adjustments informed by the specific corpus. The core analytical challenge is that Benanav's engagement with Neurath is simultaneously deep and selective: the target work explicitly builds on Neurath's multi-criterial framework and calculation-in-kind proposals while likely stripping away the epistemological infrastructure (unified science, physicalism, anti-metaphysics) and methodological commitments (ISOTYPE, empirical sociology, visual education) that made Neurath's economic proposals intelligible on their own terms. This selective engagement pattern requires: (1) deep depth on Phase 1.0 to ensure the full thematic world is reconstructed, not just the economic themes that Benanav foregrounds; (2) opus models on Phases 1-3 to handle the massive source corpus (3.6M chars) and the nuanced engagement classification work; and (3) deep depth on Phase 3.0 to capture secondary sin findings beyond the obvious primary ones. The pipeline stays strictly bounded — no expansion into thinker discovery (the source thinker is fixed as Neurath), no genealogical tracing (this is not about Benanav's intellectual development), and no multi-thinker comparison (other influences on Benanav like Keynes, Cole, or guild socialists are outside scope). The single recommended view (aoi_thematic_analysis) provides the complete reading surface with auto-included child views for source documents, by-theme, by-sin-type, and report.
